prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the vertical and forward spatial layout from the standing camera wearer's viewpoint, placing the seated client's foil-covered head and the wearer's own black-gloved hands brightest and closest at ~0.3–0.6 m below and in front (within the wearer's immediate arm's reach), with a rolling dye tray just to the lower right at ~0.5–0.8 m. Extending downward and to the left at ~0.8–1.2 m are the client's legs and held cell phone, while a second person kneels at the far lower left (~1.2–1.5 m from the wearer and within arm's reach of the client's feet, partly occluded by the left frame edge), both facing away from or perpendicular to the camera wearer so no one looks directly at the viewpoint. Behind the client at ~1.5–2.0 m are a central wall mirror flanked by left and right storage cabinets (~1.2 m apart, holding a mounted hair dryer on the left and bottles on both) and a second mirror on the far right (~2.0–2.5 m), all remaining largely static across the 5 frames while bright foreground regions expand in frames 2–5 as the wearer's gloved hands reach into view over the foils. Compared to the visually busy RGB strip, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground head, hands, and tray from the recessed floor gap (~2.0–2.5 m) beneath the mirror, though it is unreliable on the mirror surfaces—rendering the reflected client and wearer as recessed mid-range cavities rather than flat planes at the wall's depth—and blurs fine edges like the hanging dryer cord.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank in frames 1 and 2, and in frames 3–5 detects only scattered regions of the scene: the seated client at the bottom (`person`, ~0.3–0.6 m at the foil-covered head and ~0.8–1.2 m along the legs to the left), the kneeling attendant partly out of view at the lower-left edge (`person`, ~1.2–1.5 m away and within arm's reach of the client's feet), and the reflected figures in the upper central mirror (`person`, physically ~1.5–2.0 m in front). In frames 3 and 4 it also segments parts of the left storage cabinet area (~1.5–1.8 m to the left of the central mirror and ~1.0 m above the floor), labelling the wall-mounted hair dryer as `cell phone`, a top-left bottle as `bottle` (and truncated `pers`), and the cabinet body itself as `tv`, while leaving the right cabinet, right mirror, and lower-right dye tray (~0.5–0.8 m) unsegmented. Across frames 3 to 5, as the camera wearer's gloved hands move over the client's head within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) and the client remains facing forward toward the mirror away from the wearer, the bottom `person` mask appears in frame 4 and narrows in frame 5 while the left-edge attendant's mask shifts slightly as they lean over the client's lower legs. While the masks in frames 4–5 help delineate the boundary between the seated client's legs and the adjacent kneeling attendant against the cluttered floor, the map is largely unreliable because it misses all objects in frames 1–2, misclassifies the cabinet and hair dryer, treats mirror reflections as real people, omits the actual cell phone in the client's hand (~1.0 m away), and leaves unsegmented black holes over the metallic hair foils and the wearer's gloved hands.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in frames 1 through 4 and detects only a single yellow lower-body skeleton fragment near the bottom left-centre in frame 5, corresponding to the seated client's lower legs and feet (~0.8–1.2 m below and in front of the camera wearer). In the full scene context, the client sits directly below the camera wearer with their foil-covered head within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) facing the central mirror (~1.5–2.0 m ahead) and their legs stretched leftward toward a partly cropped attendant kneeling at ~1.2–1.5 m who faces the client's feet, with neither person looking toward the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's black-gloved hands enter from the bottom and right within 0.3–0.5 m to manipulate the foils next to the lower-right dye tray (~0.5–0.8 m) while the attendant works on the client's feet within the attendant's arm's reach, yet none of these hand or upper-body movements are captured by the skeleton tracker. The lone leg segment in frame 5 confirms the horizontal left-to-right orientation of the client's outstretched shins amid the overlapping cape, foil, and phone in the foreground, but the pose map is otherwise highly unreliable—failing to detect any magenta hand skeletons for the wearer's nearby gloved hands, the client's upper torso and head occluded by the salon cape and foils, the kneeling attendant on the left, or the reflected bodies in the mirrors.
